subject: Maths
title: Comparing fractions, decimals and percentages
subtitle: Decimals and Percentages · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can convert between fractions, decimals and percentages and compare their values.

key_vocab.definition: Fractions, decimals and percentages are three ways to express the same value. Convert to the same form to compare.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can convert between fractions, decimals and percentages and compare their values.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Fractions -- Fractions, decimals and percentages are three ways to express the same value. Convert to the same form to compare.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
To compare, convert all values to the same form (usually decimals or percentages).
Fraction → ÷ → Decimal → ×100 → %
Divide then multiply to convert right

Key examples:
  ✓ &frac{1}{2} = 0.5 = 50%  (half)
  ✓ &frac{1}{4} = 0.25 = 25%  (quarter)
  ✓ &frac{3}{10} = 0.3 = 30%  (three tenths)
  ✗ &frac{1}{3} = 0.3 = 30%  (0.3 repeating, not 30%)
  ✗ 0.2 = 20 (not %)  (must write 20%)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – fraction to decimal
  Convert &frac{3}{8} to a decimal.
  Divide numerator by denominator: 3 ÷ 8
  = 0.375
  So &frac{3}{8} = 0.375
  = 0.375
  (Fraction means numerator divided by denominator.)

Example 2 – decimal to percentage
  Convert 0.45 to a percentage.
  Multiply by 100
  0.45 × 100 = 45
  = 45%
  = 45%
  (Move the decimal point two places right.)

sections.content:

(b) ? fraction = 0.4 = ? %
(c) ? fraction = ? decimal = 85%
(d) &frac{7}{8} = ? decimal = ? %
(e) ? fraction = 0.15 = ? %

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ &frac{1}{2} = 0.5 = 50%
✗ 0.4 = 4%
✓ To convert decimal to %, multiply by 100
✗ &frac{1}{3} = 33%
✓ 75% = &frac{3}{4}
